results.scenario: bandmates responding to an unexpectedly large festival slot
results.trigger_note: A has committed the band to play a main-stage show for ten thousand people.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: The festival coordinator called right after rehearsal.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Our little afternoon slot disappeared because another act canceled.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: She offered us the main stage, but she needed an answer tonight.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I told her we'd play Saturday in front of ten thousand people.

version_1.response: You're right, I got carried away. I'll call her back and withdraw before she locks us in.

version_2.response: Okay, I'll confirm the slot and book us extra rehearsals every night this week.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: The gasp reads as alarm at taking on an overwhelming performance, so A backs out; the grunt reads as a reluctant go-ahead, so A commits and prepares.

judge.notes: The weakest property is interpretations_fit_the_context, since a gasp could also convey surprise or excitement rather than specifically fear.

results.scenario: neighbors discovering a banner-printing mistake before a park cleanup
results.trigger_note: Fifty public banners contain an embarrassing slogan typo.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I picked up the banners for Saturday's park cleanup.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I gave the print shop the slogan exactly as the committee wrote it.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: They were supposed to say, "Keep Our Park Clean."

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Instead, all fifty say, "Keep Our Pants Clean," and they're already hanging across Main Street.

version_1.response: I'll call the shop now and get those banners taken down before anyone else sees them.

version_2.response: All right, the banners stay—we'll make the typo the cleanup's running joke.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: A gasp treats the public mistake as an urgent embarrassment that needs fixing, while laughter makes it reasonable to embrace the absurdity instead of removing the banners.

judge.notes: The weakest property is undecidable_from_text_alone, since the public embarrassment somewhat independently favors taking the banners down, though either response remains plausible.

results.scenario: roommates deciding how to handle an expensive dishwasher repair
results.trigger_note: The repair estimate is far higher than expected.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I heard back from the appliance shop about our dishwasher.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: The pump is cracked, but they can get the part tomorrow.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Buying a new machine would mean waiting at least two weeks for delivery.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Their repair estimate is eight hundred and forty dollars.

version_1.response: Hold off on the repair—I’m calling around for a cheaper quote before we spend that.

version_2.response: Yeah, we can’t keep doing dishes in the sink; I’ll authorize the repair today.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: The gasp suggests the price is too startling to accept without challenging it, while the sigh suggests weary acceptance of an unwanted but necessary repair.

judge.notes: The weakest property is undecidable_from_text_alone, since the high repair estimate somewhat favors seeking another quote even without the vocalization.

results.trigger_note: The observatory will open its roof for a meteor shower viewing.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I've been trying to find something different for Friday night.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: The old observatory has started doing late-night programs again.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Usually it's an hour of slides about constellations.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: But this Friday they're opening the roof so people can watch the meteor shower.

version_1.response: Then I'm booking us spots before that viewing deck fills up.

version_2.response: All right, I'll drop the observatory idea and find us something with more energy.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: A gasp makes the meteor shower sound exciting enough to book immediately, while a yawn signals that the observatory program is not an appealing outing and prompts A to choose a different plan.

judge.notes: The weakest property is whether a yawn is natural, since the meteor-shower reveal is framed as an appealing activity, though disinterest in astronomy remains plausible.

results.scenario: coworkers reviewing an accidental email sign-off
results.trigger_note: A says the client received the email signed with a childish nickname.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I sent the revised budget to the client before lunch.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I copied the numbers straight from finance, so at least the totals are right.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: But I wrote it on my phone while I was waiting for the elevator.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: My email signature went out as “Captain Spreadsheet.”

version_1.response: You're right, I’ll send a clean follow-up from my laptop and apologize for the signature.

version_2.response: Okay, that is objectively funny—I’m leaving it alone unless the client mentions it.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: The grunt reads the mistaken sign-off as unprofessional and calls for immediate correction, while the laughter treats it as harmlessly funny and supports letting it stand.

judge.notes: The weakest property is voc2_favors_reply2, since genuine laughter could still be followed by a decision to correct the signature.

results.scenario: siblings deciding how to handle a crack in a bedroom wall
results.trigger_note: The contractor says the wall crack is not structural.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: The contractor finally came to look at the crack above the window.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I showed him how much wider it got after last week's rain.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: He checked the wall from outside and climbed up into the attic.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: He says it's only peeling plaster, not a structural crack.

version_1.response: I won't have anyone patch it yet; I'll get a structural engineer to inspect it before we touch that wall.

version_2.response: Then I'll cancel the structural engineer and ask the painter to patch it this week.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: The grunt is taken as doubt about the contractor's diagnosis, so A seeks an independent structural inspection. The sigh is taken as relief that the wall is safe, so A cancels the extra inspection and proceeds with a cosmetic repair.

judge.notes: The weakest property is undecidable_from_text_alone, since the contractor's reassurance somewhat favors the relief-and-patch response even though caution remains plausible.

results.scenario: roommates learning that a disputed apartment application was approved
results.trigger_note: A says they accepted B's apartment offer without asking first.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I finally got through to the housing office about the application they rejected.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: They found out the income form had been filed under somebody else's name.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: That mix-up was the only reason they turned you down.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: They've offered you the unit, and I told them you'd take it before I called.

version_1.response: You're right, I shouldn't have answered for you. I'll call back and put the offer on hold until you've decided.

version_2.response: I'll book the lease-signing appointment now, then we can start moving your boxes over tonight.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: The grunt reads as objection to A making the decision unilaterally, so A pauses the offer. The sob reads as overwhelmed relief that the appeal succeeded, so A moves ahead with securing the apartment.

judge.notes: The weakest property is voc2_favors_reply2, since relieved sobbing does not conclusively establish consent to immediately book the lease signing.

results.trigger_note: The manager requires them to stay late for training on two consecutive nights.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I checked with the manager about the new register system.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: The training videos can only be accessed after we close.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: We both have to complete them before next week's audit.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: She wants us to stay two extra hours tonight and tomorrow to finish them.

version_1.response: All right, I'll get us dinner, and we'll stay to knock the videos out tonight.

version_2.response: No, I’m not keeping us here when we’re already worn out; I’ll ask her to schedule the training during a staffed shift next week.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: The grunt is read as resigned willingness to accept the late work, so A commits to completing it that night. The yawn signals that the extra evening work is too exhausting, so A rejects the after-hours plan and seeks a daytime alternative.

judge.notes: The weakest property is that a yawn is only an indirect cue of fatigue, though the proposed extra late work makes it natural.

results.scenario: friends volunteering together at a community fair
results.trigger_note: A reveals that their volunteer shift is running a dunk tank in matching pirate costumes.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: The community fair still needed two people for an afternoon shift.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I told Dana that you and I could volunteer together.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: She said teams can switch booths until noon if something really doesn't suit them.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: She assigned us to run the dunk tank in matching pirate costumes.

version_1.response: Then we’re owning it—I’ll bring eye patches, and we’ll make that dunk tank the best booth there.

version_2.response: Okay, I should have checked with you first; I’ll ask Dana to move us to a quieter booth before noon.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: Laughter supports embracing the absurd costume assignment, while a sigh signals that the assignment is unwelcome, so A requests a different shift.

judge.notes: The weakest property is both_vocalizations_natural_here, since the sigh is somewhat less strongly motivated than the laughter but remains plausible.

results.scenario: siblings preparing a birthday slideshow from old family videos
results.trigger_note: A recovered a lost clip of their late father singing badly and expressing love.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I've been sorting through the old camcorder files for Mom's birthday slideshow.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Most of them are blurry holidays, with everybody talking over each other.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I thought the recording from the year Dad died had been lost for good.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: But I found one where he's singing "Happy Birthday" hopelessly off-key, then he looks at Mom and says, "I love you, June."

version_1.response: Then I'm putting that clip at the end of the slideshow—his terrible singing will make everyone smile.

version_2.response: I'll keep that one out of the slideshow and save it for just us after the party.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: Laughter supports sharing the clip publicly as a warm, funny memory, while sobbing suggests it is too emotionally personal for the party and should be kept private.

judge.notes: The weakest property is both_vocalizations_natural_here, since laughter is somewhat less immediate than a sob after recalling Dad's death, though the off-key singing makes affectionate amusement plausible.

results.trigger_note: A has made a forty-minute dramatic video for a quick volunteer tour.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I promised the new volunteers a quick tour of the storage room before they start.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: While I was cleaning, I found the security clips from last year's costume drive.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Most of them are just people trying to squeeze giant donation boxes through the door.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I stitched them into a forty-minute video with dramatic narration.

version_1.response: Perfect, I’ll keep the full cut and use it to open the orientation.

version_2.response: Right, I’ll shelve the video and give them the two-minute tour instead.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: Laughter supports treating the absurd video as entertaining enough to feature, while a yawn signals that its length would lose the audience, so A abandons it for a concise tour.

judge.notes: The weakest property is undecidable_from_text_alone, since the earlier promise of a quick tour mildly favors shelving a forty-minute video even without the vocalization.

results.scenario: classmates deciding whether to continue a retiring teacher's garden club
results.trigger_note: A teacher has entrusted them with the keys and notebook for the garden club.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I stopped by the school greenhouse after class.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Ms. Chen was clearing out her desk; the district is making her retire at the end of the month.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: She said the garden club will disappear unless someone takes it over.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: She put the keys and her whole planting notebook in my hands.

version_1.response: You're right, we already have too much on our plates. I'll take the keys back and tell her we can't run it.

version_2.response: Then we'll keep it going. I'll message the club tonight, and we'll make sure Ms. Chen's garden doesn't disappear.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: The sigh reads the handoff as an unsustainable new burden, so A declines it; the sob reads it as a moving trust from Ms. Chen, so A commits to preserving the club.

judge.notes: The weakest property is whether a sob is fully natural here, since the situation is poignant but could be less immediately sob-inducing for some listeners.

results.scenario: coworkers discovering a duplicate-entry requirement for old receipts
results.trigger_note: Every receipt must be entered twice in separate systems.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: We've been sorting these old donation receipts since breakfast.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I finally opened the instructions for putting them into the new system.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I thought we were nearly finished with the stack.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: It turns out every receipt has to be typed twice, once for the archive and once for accounting.

version_1.response: No, that is a broken process. I'll call accounting and get permission to use one shared file.

version_2.response: We're stopping for today; I'll lock these up, and we can finish after you've had some sleep.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: The sigh reads as frustration with an inefficient requirement, so A challenges the process. The yawn reads as exhaustion from the long work session, so A stops the work instead.

judge.notes: The weakest property is swapping_replies_is_clearly_worse, since frustration could also reasonably lead to stopping work for the day.

results.scenario: friends editing a retirement tribute video late at night
results.trigger_note: A former student's message reveals that the teacher paid for a bus pass so he could stay in school.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I've been editing Ms. Patel's retirement video since after dinner.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: It's nearly midnight, and I still have sixty-seven clips open.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I wanted your help deciding what deserves the last few minutes.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Her first student sent this: “You bought my bus pass so I could stay in school.”

version_1.response: That message is the ending, then—I’ll keep the whole clip, even if the video runs long.

version_2.response: I've kept you up too late; I’ll save this now and make a short cut in the morning.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: A sob makes the message feel important enough to preserve in full, while a yawn signals that the late-night editing session should stop and be shortened later.

judge.notes: The weakest property is undecidable_from_text_alone, since the emotional content of the quoted message somewhat favors keeping the clip even without the vocalization.
